title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 85-87): L is an ordered set, playing the role of a 'line'. M = M(L) is a combinatorial model of the line whose elements ('lieux') are of two kinds: points P_x (x in L), forming M_0, and open segments S_{a,b} (a<b), forming M_1. The page uses three relations between elements: X |o| Y (interiors disjoint), X || Y (closures disjoint, i.e. strongly separated), and X ≍ Y (overlap). The negation X ≭ Y is the 'compatibility' condition: X and Y may sit together in a 'figure', i.e. a finite cell decomposition. On the previous page Grothendieck showed that M is faithful iff L is totally ordered.

On this page he turns to 'questions de support' and first studies finite figures. He makes the compatibility relation explicit.
(1) If one of the elements is a point: P_x ≭ Y iff P_x = Y or P_x |o| Y. Hence P_x ≭ P_y forces {x,y} to be a totally ordered (comparable) finite subset of L, i.e. {x,y} ∈ Dnp(L). Also P_x ≭ S_{a,b} iff P_x |o| S_{a,b} iff x ≤ a or x ≥ b.
(2) Two segments are compatible iff one of three things holds:
- they are equal;
- they are strictly separated (S || S');
- their closures meet only inside ∂S ∩ ∂S', in a nonempty set, while their interiors are disjoint.
In the third case ∂S ∩ ∂S' is a single element. If it had two elements then ∂S = ∂S' = {a,b}, hence S = S', which is the first case.
The result is: S_{a,b} ≭ S_{a',b'} iff (i) a=a', b=b'; or (ii) a<b<a'<b' or a'<b'<a<b; or (iii) a<b≤a'<b' or the symmetric case. This condenses to S ≭ S' iff S = S' or S |o| S', i.e. a<b≤a'<b' or a'<b'≤a<b.

On the next page this feeds into the 'boundary set' δX ⊂ L (card 1 or 2). The necessary condition is that δX ∪ δY is a finite totally ordered subset. He then introduces 'interstitial' segments and points of a finite chain T ⊂ L, i.e. the finite figures are the cell decompositions of the line given by finite chains. This is the 1-dimensional base case of his combinatorial/tame 'analysis situs' of loci and supports.
errors: Machine transcription has 'x ≤ a ou a ≥ b'; the intended (and visible) condition is x ≤ a or x ≥ b. This is a transcription slip, not a mathematical error.

Minor sloppiness: P_x ≭ P_y should give {x,y} totally ordered even when x=y (a singleton), which is fine. Without total order of L the stated equivalence 'P_x ≭ Y ⟺ P_x = Y or P_x |o| Y' is asserted as holding for loci 'dans un ...' (a qualifier is partly illegible). No genuine mathematical error found; the case analysis is correct for totally ordered L.

ideas.what: Compatibility (equal or interior-disjoint) of cells in a combinatorial model of the line built from points and open segments of an ordered set
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / stratification of a 1-dimensional ordered space; face poset of a subdivided interval; o-minimal 1-dim cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (CW/simplicial subdivisions); o-minimal cell decomposition by van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the detailed Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Boundary-intersection lemma: two distinct segments share at most one boundary element
ideas.modern_name: Elementary property of intervals in a total order

ideas.what: Finite figures in L correspond to finite chains (Dnp(L)) with their interstitial points and segments (developed on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision of the line by a finite set; nerve/face poset of an ordered finite set

deep.surprise_reason: A routine case analysis of compatibility for points and segments of a totally ordered set. It is the 1-dimensional base case of Grothendieck's axiomatic 'analysis situs' of loci. It is interesting only as documentation of how he set up the combinatorial tame-topology framework; there is no new result here.
transcription_corrections: 'x ≤ a ou a ≥ b' should read 'x ≤ a ou x ≥ b'.
'Disp(L)' is likely 'Dnp(L)' (finite totally ordered subsets of L), consistent with the next page.
Case (ii) in the image appears as 'a<b<a'<b' ou a'<b'<a<b', and case (iii) as 'a<b ≤ a'<b' ou a'<b' ≤ a<b' (with a struck-through symbol). The final line likewise reads 'a<b ≤ a'<b' ou a'<b' ≤ a<b'.
'cas pas non envisagé' is probably 'cas pas envisagé ici' (the equal case is excluded).
The phrase 'supports réduits sur L, faute de Mog L 2' is uncertain. It may be 'supports induits sur L'; the following words are illegible in the machine reading.
